jobs.title: Director Application, Data & Integration
jobs.description:
Director, Application, Data & Integration

Location:
Vancouver, BC

Salary Range:
$159,000 - $215,000/year

Ready to take the next step in your career with a firm that values innovation, collaboration, continuous improvement, and delivering exceptional client experiences?

Smythe LLP is seeking an experienced and strategic Director, Application, Data & Integration
to join our growing Digital Business Services (DBS) team. This is an exceptional opportunity for a technology leader who is passionate about building modern application, data, and integration capabilities while helping shape the future of technology across the firm.

This role is based in our Vancouver office, with the opportunity to work in a hybrid environment following the completion of the probationary period.

The Opportunity

The Director, Application, Data & Integration is responsible for building and leading Smythe’s enterprise application, data and integration capabilities.

The role provides technical leadership across the firm’s application landscape and establishes the engineering disciplines required to deliver secure, reliable and maintainable solutions. A key mandate is to transform how the development team works through AI-assisted engineering, automation and modern DevOps practices, driving significant improvements in development productivity and delivery speed.

The Director will also build Smythe’s data engineering and analytics capabilities and lead the integration architecture that connects the firm’s core systems. This is a capability-building leadership role supporting Smythe’s Connected Firm strategy and continued technology modernization.

In This Role, You Will

Application Strategy & Architecture

Provide technical leadership and architecture oversight across Smythe’s enterprise application landscape.
Establish application architecture, development and lifecycle standards.
Guide solution design for new applications and major enhancements.
Partner with Product Owners to translate business requirements into sustainable technical solutions.
Provide technical oversight of implementation partners and third-party development resources.

Engineering Discipline, DevOps & AI-Assisted Development

Build and mature Smythe’s software engineering practices, including development standards, source control, code review, testing and documentation.
Establish CI/CD, environment and release-management capabilities to enable controlled and repeatable deployments.
Embed application security and secure development practices throughout the software development lifecycle.
Lead adoption of AI-assisted development across the engineering team to accelerate development, testing, documentation and delivery.
Drive significant, multi-fold improvements in engineering productivity while maintaining appropriate security, quality and human oversight.
Strengthen automated testing, application monitoring and overall technical quality.

Integration & Connected Firm Architecture

Own Smythe’s integration architecture and technical integration standards.
Establish consistent approaches for APIs, interfaces and system-to-system data exchange.
Ensure integrations across the application landscape are secure, resilient, supportable and appropriately monitored.
Maintain an architectural view of how applications, integrations and data work together to support the Connected Firm.

Dynamics & DPO Technical Leadership

Provide technical leadership for Smythe’s transition to Dynamics 365 Project Operations and the broader Dynamics platform.
Work with Product Owners and implementation partners on architecture, integration and technical design.
Build sufficient internal capability to support, maintain and extend the platform over time.
Ensure Dynamics development follows Smythe’s engineering, security and application-management standards.

Data Management, Engineering & Analytics

Develop Smythe’s enterprise data architecture and technical data-management approach.
Build data engineering capabilities to integrate, transform and make trusted data available across the firm.
Establish approaches for master data, data quality, lineage and technical data controls.
Build and lead the firm’s emerging data engineering and data analytics capabilities.
Enable consistent enterprise reporting and analytics.
Partner with Product Owners and business stakeholders on data ownership and governance.

People & Capability Leadership

Build and lead capabilities spanning application development, integration, QA, data engineering and analytics.
Develop technical staff and establish clear engineering expectations and practices.
Determine the appropriate balance of internal capabilities, implementation partners and specialized contractors.
Build a culture focused on technical quality, accountability, continuous improvement and effective use of AI-assisted development.

Security, Risk & Operational Partnership

Partner with IT Operations to ensure applications and integrations meet Smythe’s security, resilience and operational requirements.
Embed security-by-design into application architecture and engineering practices.
Ensure solutions incorporate appropriate access, data protection, monitoring and operational support requirements.

What You Bring

Progressive technology leadership experience across enterprise applications, software engineering, integration and data.
Demonstrated experience building or maturing software engineering and DevOps practices.
Strong understanding of modern application architecture, APIs, integrations and cloud platforms.
Practical experience with CI/CD, automated testing, secure development and application lifecycle management.
Experience adopting modern development practices and AI-assisted development tools to materially improve engineering productivity and software delivery.
Experience with data architecture, data engineering, analytics or business intelligence.
Experience leading multidisciplinary technical teams and external technology partners.
Microsoft technology and Dynamics 365 experience is strongly preferred.
Strong communication skills with the ability to work effectively with both technical teams and business leaders.

Leadership Characteristics

The Successful Candidate Will

Be a builder, comfortable creating and scaling capabilities that do not yet fully exist.
Bring strong engineering discipline while remaining pragmatic about business delivery.
Be forward-looking in the use of AI and automation to fundamentally improve how technology is delivered.
Set high technical standards without introducing unnecessary complexity or bureaucracy.
Develop people and internal capability while using external partners effectively.
Communicate complex technical concepts clearly to business and executive stakeholders.

What Smythe Offers

At Smythe, we strive to offer a competitive salary and benefits package that accurately reflects our people’s values and ambitions. We prioritize professional development and have fostered a dynamic and progressive work culture. As a firm, our focus is on collaboration and building personal relationships with clients, mentors and peers. Learn more about what you can expect from Life at Smythe by visiting our website (www.smythecpa.com) and following us on Instagram (@lifeatsmythe) and LinkedIn (@Smythe LLP).

We thank you for your interest in joining Smythe! We will get back to you regarding any updates to your application.

jobs.title: Director of Computer Vision
jobs.description:
Company Overview

At Motorola Solutions, we believe that everything starts with our people. We’re a global close-knit community, united by the relentless pursuit to help keep people safer everywhere. We build and connect technologies to help protect people, property and places. Our solutions foster the collaboration that’s critical for safer communities, safer schools, safer hospitals, safer businesses, and ultimately, safer nations. Connect with a career that matters, and help us build a safer future.

Aperçu de l’entreprise

Chez Motorola Solutions, nous pensons que tout commence par nos employés. Nous sommes une communauté mondiale soudée, unie par la volonté incessante de contribuer à la sécurité des personnes partout dans le monde. Nous concevons et connectons des technologies qui contribuent à protéger les personnes, les biens et les infrastructures. Nos solutions favorisent la collaboration essentielle pour améliorer la sécurité des populations, des écoles, des hôpitaux, des entreprises et, finalement, des nations. Connectez-vous à une carrière qui compte et aidez-nous à bâtir un avenir plus sûr.

Department Overview

Motorola Solutions' innovations, products, and services play essential roles in people's lives. Our end-to-end suite of software solutions helps customers manage emergency communications, process video and evidence, and leverage cutting-edge AI-driven analytics for security and operational insights. We are industry leaders in video security and analytics, with solutions deployed in more than 120 countries across diverse environments such as school campuses, transportation systems, healthcare centers, public venues, critical infrastructure, prisons, factories, casinos, airports, financial institutions, government facilities, and retailers. Our AI-powered security solutions integrate advanced video analytics, machine learning, and embedded intelligence to enable proactive threat detection, enhanced situational awareness, and automated decision-making.

Job Description

Job DescriptionThe Director of Computer Vision will drive the technical vision, research and engineering execution for the platform, with focus on the following core areas:

Foundational Research Strategy: Define the long-term research agenda for fundamental computer vision capabilities and drive the culture of scientific excellence.
Technical Vision, Engineering Leadership, and Execution: Provide executive technical leadership to a unified research and engineering organization, defining the technical architecture, strategy, and engineering roadmap for the Computer Vision Platform. Drive execution, ensuring the seamless translation of product requirements into robust technical specifications and successful delivery of next-generation visual intelligence solutions that are highly scalable and align with overall product and business strategy.
Organizational Leadership and Talent Strategy: Manage and scale a unified computer vision research and engineering organization distributed across multiple geographies, overseeing multiple teams, and defining the strategy for recruiting, mentoring, and attracting world-class talent.
End-to-End MLOps and Deployment: Own the entire engineering lifecycle for central, reusable computer vision models and foundational AI infrastructure. This includes establishing best-in-class MLOps practices for scalable training, efficient deployment, continuous monitoring, and performance optimization across edge and cloud environments.
Performance Measurement and Continuous Improvement: Define, implement, and track key technical performance metrics (e.g., latency, throughput, model efficiency, system reliability) to measure engineering success, identify bottlenecks, and drive continuous improvement in execution and delivery.
Technical Innovation and Risk Management: Evaluate and integrate cutting-edge computer vision research and technologies. Proactively identify and mitigate significant technical risks, and lead critical engineering decisions, including build-versus-buy analysis.

Qualifications & Experience

10+ years of technical leadership experience leading computer vision teams and organizations, with a focus on building and deploying enterprise-scale platforms and solutions in production.
Technical Acumen & Deep Expertise: Deep, demonstrable expertise in computer vision, machine learning algorithms, and the end-to-end MLOps lifecycle, including 5+ years of hands-on experience building and optimizing computer vision models or as a computer vision researcher. Proven ability to engage in complex technical discussions, define the architectural vision for central, reusable AI infrastructure and models, and drive technical strategy while managing critical trade-offs.
Executive Technical Strategy & Metrics: Proven experience defining long-term technical vision, engineering strategy, and roadmaps for a large-scale platform. Expertise in defining and implementing technical metrics (e.g., latency, throughput, system reliability, model efficiency) to measure engineering excellence and drive continuous improvement across an organization.
Organizational & People Leadership: Demonstrated ability to manage and scale a unified, distributed engineering and research organization of 50 to 100 people, mentor senior technical talent, and lead multiple teams across different geographies.
Strong Analytical and Research Skills: Hands-on experience driving innovation through foundational research, working with AI performance metrics (e.g., Precision/Recall), real-time video processing, and inference optimization.
Customer-Driven Technical Leadership (Pathfinding): Track record of translating highly ambiguous product concepts and complex customer needs into clear, executable technical roadmaps and architectural specifications.
Start-up Mentality & Agility: Experience in a start-up or fast-paced environment is highly valued, demonstrating high ownership, bias for action, comfort with ambiguity, and the ability to drive 0-to-1 product development with limited resources.
Domain Knowledge: Experience in public safety, security-focused software (e.g., video security, evidence management), mission-critical systems, or emergency communications is a plus.

Target Base Salary Range: $230,000 CAD - $270,000 CAD

Consistent with Motorola Solutions values and applicable law, we provide the following information to promote pay transparency and equity. Pay within this range varies and depends on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. The actual offer will be based on the individual candidate.

Note: Candidates must reside in a Canada within the Eastern (EST) or Central (CST) Time Zone.

Basic Requirements

Bachelors degree with 10+ years of technical leadership experience leading computer vision teams and organizations.

Travel Requirements

10-25%

Relocation Provided

None

Position Type

Experienced

Referral Payment Plan

No

EEO Statement

Motorola Solutions is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion or belief, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status or any other legally-protected characteristic.

We are proud of our people-first and community-focused culture, empowering every Motorolan to be their most authentic self and to do their best work to deliver on the promise of a safer world. If you’d like to join our team but feel that you don’t quite meet all of the preferred skills, we’d still love to hear why you think you’d be a great addition to our team.

We’re committed to providing an inclusive and accessible recruiting experience for candidates with disabilities, or other physical or mental health conditions. To request an accommodation, please complete this Reasonable Accommodations Form so we can assist you.

Motorola Solutions adopte, favorise et promeut les principes de diversité, d’équité et d’inclusion. Nous encourageons et accueillons les candidatures de toutes les personnes qualifiées, quelles que soient leur race, origines ethnique, religion ou croyance, orientation sexuelle, identité et expression sexuelle, statut d’anciens combattants ou tout autre statut protégé par la Loi.

Nous sommes fiers de notre culture axée sur les personnes et les communautés, encourageant ainsi chaque Motorolan d’être la version la plus authentique de lui-même dans ses responsabilités afin de tenir la promesse d’un monde plus sécuritaire.

Si vous souhaitez vous joindre à notre communauté mais croyez que vous ne possédez pas toutes les exigences requises pour le poste convoité, nous aimerions tout de même connaître les raisons pour lesquelles vous pensez être un excellent candidat pour notre équipe.

Nous offrons également des mesures d’adaptation pendant toutes les étapes du processus d’embauche afin de favoriser l’inclusion des personnes vivant avec un handicap physique et/ou mental. Pour demander un aménagement, veuillez remplir ce formulaire d'aménagement raisonnable afin que nous puissions vous aider.

Director, Customer Services and Informatics

The midpoint of the range is approximately halfway between the minimum and the maximum and represents an employee that possesses full job knowledge, qualifications and experience for the position. In the normal course, employees will be hired, transferred or promoted between the minimum and midpoint of the salary range for a job.

Job End Date

Ongoing

Posting End Date

December 9, 2026

Note:
Applications will be accepted until 11:59 PM on the Posting End Date.

At UBC, we believe that attracting and sustaining a diverse workforce is key to the successful pursuit of excellence in research, innovation, and learning for all faculty, staff and students. Our commitment to employment equity helps achieve inclusion and fairness, brings rich diversity to UBC as a workplace, and creates the necessary conditions for a rewarding career.

Job Description Summary

The Director of Customer Services and Informatics is a senior leadership position within UBC Facilities. The Director provides strategic leadership for Facilities customer service function, customer service plan, business project management, business analysis, informatics, enterprise maintenance management system (EMMS), facilities information and inventory systems, change management, call centre management and clerical support services. This role develops strategic objectives, implements and monitors procedures and policies that enable Facilities to meet or exceed agreed customer service standards across the entire campus. In addition, this division provides all business units within Facilities the necessary business support both by providing the necessary analytics and analysis to ensure continuous improvements continue across the department. The Director is responsible for the development and sustainment of the Facilities Emergency Management Plan.

The Director of Customer Services and Informatics is the Facilities representative for customer engagement, business projects and initiatives, space inventory data, building and infrastructure records drawings and information, analytics, reporting, technology and continuous improvement initiatives. They partner with Information Technology (IT) and Safety and Risk Services (SRS) - Emergency Management, Project Management Office (PMO), Integrated Service Centre (ISC), Communications & Engagement for strategic alignment and resource allocation.

The Director leads a workforce of approximately 35 staff in professional and unionized positions. Prepares strategic and business plans and supports an annual Facilities budget of approximately $150M.

Organizational Status

This position reports directly to the Associate Vice-President, Facilities, and serves as a member of the Facilities Leadership team. Works closely with other Directors, Senior Managers, and Managers as well as other department‘s leadership teams. This position is the senior leader within Facilities responsible for implementing business transformational initiatives with the support of other divisions, monitoring operational progress through the analysis and reporting of information to guide evidence-based decision-making.

Work Performed

Provides strategic leadership to the Facilities Leadership team through the Customer Services and Informatics division to execute a full range of department-wide services to meet targets and objectives of the Strategic Plan. This includes supporting and developing business plans; ensuring consistent and effective implementation; enhancing integration; standardizing services and business practices; maximizing efficiencies and cost savings.
Responsible for business transformational projects through assessment, analysis, design and implementation; champions the implementation of change management initiatives, process and execution.
Leads the development of a Monitoring Framework with key performance indicators for each unit within the department and develops remedial and continuous improvement plans in relation to results. This framework includes leading and lagging indicators and an effective client satisfaction monitoring and reporting system to evaluate the services provided by the entire Facilities group.
Leads the facilities information and inventory systems function, including university space inventory data, building and infrastructure record drawings, key plans, emergency response plans, and maintenance manuals.
Provides direction and implements change management methodologies to effectively lead and optimize key projects across Facilities.
Mentors and coaches change management in relation to the implementation of business initiatives.
Liaises with academic, administrative and ancillary customers, engineers, architects and external clients to ensure that the facilities needs of the university are being met.
Supports and provides direction to the Senior Facilities Manager in providing strategic leadership to the Facilities Managers working in the geographic zone model. Through the Senior Facilities Manager, oversees the delivery of equal, consistent and effectively prioritized service delivery within the campus zones.
Provides strategic leadership on sustainment of Facilities and University information systems in support of enterprise maintenance management, asset management, stores inventory, space inventory, records drawings, records management, and project management.
Provides strategic leadership and/or oversees development of innovative business solutions and services that integrate data and reporting capabilities to augment decision-making.
Oversees work of various teams performing quality testing of data and information and reconciling across sources, presenting facts and evidence in dashboards to assist in effective evidence-based decision making.
Provides strategic leadership to the Facilities Service Centre who are responsible for handling inbound and outbound calls regarding buildings and grounds.
Responsible for administrative/clerical support services for the Facilities group.
Provides direction in the completion of regulatory and skills development training for all staff within Facilities which includes developing plans, implementing and evaluating, department-wide strategies.
Leads and directs the development of the Facilities Emergency Management Plan, including emergency preparedness exercises for the department in collaboration with SRS, Emergency Management.
Works with SRS and implements consistent health, safety and environmental initiatives, which, includes safety committee, accident investigations, safety training and safety recommendations within the Customer Services and Informatics division.
Responsible for human resource practices including recruitment, orientation, training, performance evaluation, discipline, labor relations and dismissal within the Customer Services and Informatics division in collaboration with Human Resources.
Performs other related duties, including but not limited to:
Representing Facilities on various university committees. Develops working relationships and partnerships with key stakeholders across UBC.
Acting on behalf of the Associate Vice-President, Facilities.

Consequence of Error/Judgement

Facilities plays a key role in enabling the University to achieve its goal of becoming one of the world‘s leading universities. The Director Customer Services and Informatics position is critical to the success of Facilities and the complex services that it provides. The Director must apply judgment, tact and discretion due to the broad and extensive implications for success in the areas of facilities management, project management, business analysis, informatics, information system management, change management, call centre management and clerical support services. The Director plays an important part in the formulation, alignment and implementation of the strategic initiatives and managing the outcomes and impacts on operations and the services they provide.

Failure to ensure alignment and direction for Facilities in this role will negatively impact on the reputation of the University. The consequence of poor decisions have human resources, legal and representational consequences and in addition to costs. Failure to effectively direct major projects that transform business operations through change or to ensure accurate asset information for facilities planning, major capital decisions, or maintenance, construction and renovation activities will lead to the loss of millions of dollars in investment, inefficiencies or unrealized efficiency benefits, and potential safety issues.

Supervision Received

Works autonomously within broad objectives under the senior administrative direction of the Associate Vice-President, Facilities.

Supervision Given

The Director of Customer Services and Informatics manages a workforce of approximately 35 employees. The Director is directly responsible for supervising work of 6 professional staff in manager and senior manager roles, with a diverse portfolio of supporting units including the areas of facilities management, project management, business analysis, informatics, facilities information and inventory systems, change management, call centre management and clerical support services. This position will also act as the Associate Vice-President, Facilities from time to time.

Minimum Qualifications

Undergraduate degree in a relevant discipline. Eligibility for membership in a professional Institute or Association. Minimum of 9 years of related experience, or the equivalent combination of education and experience.

Willingness to respect diverse perspectives, including perspectives in conflict with one’s own
Demonstrates a commitment to enhancing one’s own awareness, knowledge, and skills related to equity, diversity, and inclusion

Preferred Qualifications

Eligibility for membership in a professional Institute or Association. Master of Business Administration or equivalent preferred. 12 years experience or an equivalent combination of education and experience in transforming businesses within complex unionized environments preferred.
Significant experience in areas of strategic planning, tactical planning, change management, project management, risk management, information system management, business process improvement, critical and systems thinking, continuous improvement, quality assurance, adult education and maintenance, operations management and organizational design would be advantageous.
Formal education in Project Management and/or a Project Management Professional (PMP) designation or another relevant discipline is an asset. Proven ability to initiate, plan and execute business projects.
Experience working in a complex, multi-departmental organization.
Experienced in leadership development, facilitation, coaching and mentoring.
Significant experience in leading large-scale transformation and change initiatives within complex, multi-union environments.
Strong leadership skills with emphasis on decision-making, problem solving, consulting, marketing, facilitation, negotiation and team-building skills and the ability to foster a motivating and respectful work environment.
Strong interpersonal and oral and written communication skills, emphasizing listening, and negotiating; bargaining, compromising, and conciliation; ability to summarize needs, determine priorities and necessities
Demonstrated leadership and organizational abilities; mature judgment, ability to make decisions under time constraints, managing risk and uncertainty, multi-tasking, and ability to set priorities.

jobs.title: Vice President, Operations
jobs.description:
Description

Poste chez Vision Group

VICE PRESIDENT, OPERATIONS

Lead performance. Develop leaders. Shape the future of clinic operations.

Working at Vision Group’s head office means joining one of North America’s leading vision correction providers. You will contribute to the growth of an organization supporting more than 11 brands and 60 clinics across Canada and the United States.

Join our team, where our Great Place to Work® certification reflects our commitment to creating a supportive and inclusive workplace.

Your Mandate

The Vice President of Operations leads the operational performance and ongoing development of Vision Group’s national clinic network. Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, this executive translates business strategy into consistent clinic execution, strengthens operational leadership, and builds a scalable operating model that supports exceptional patient care and sustainable growth.

The mandate centres on four priorities: performance, people, patient flow, and execution. Working closely with clinical and corporate partners, the Vice President aligns resources, operating standards, and management practices to drive consistent performance while responding to regional needs and clinical realities.

The position requires regular travel across the clinic network.

Your tasks at a glance

Operational Strategy and Performance

Develop and execute the clinic operations strategy in alignment with organizational priorities.
Establish operational goals, budgets, performance indicators, and accountability across regional, district, and clinic leadership.
Oversee productivity, capacity utilization, labour efficiency, conversion, patient experience, and operating costs.
Translate financial and operational data into actionable insights, corrective plans, and measurable improvements.
Establish consistent performance reviews and follow-up practices across the network.

Leadership and Organizational Development

Lead, coach, and develop Regional and District Operations leaders, strengthening their ability to deliver results through clinic teams.
Establish clear expectations, effective delegation, and consistent performance management across the operations organization.
Partner with Talent & Culture on workforce planning, leadership development, succession planning, and employee engagement.
Build a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement, ensuring leaders have the tools and support to succeed.

Patient Flow and Capacity Optimization

Align clinic staffing, scheduling, and capacity with patient demand and business priorities.
Improve the patient journey from consultation and pre-operative assessment through surgery and post-operative follow-up.
Address bottlenecks affecting patient access, experience, throughput, and conversion in partnership with Medical Affairs and clinical leaders, while respecting clinical judgment and patient safety.

Operating Model and Continuous Improvement

Develop scalable operating standards, processes, and management practices, balancing network-wide consistency with local requirements.
Identify effective practices, support their adoption across clinics, and measure their sustained impact.
Partner with Technology and Business Intelligence to improve reporting, decision-making, and operational workflows.

Transformation, Integration, and Growth

Lead the operational delivery of transformation initiatives, clinic integrations, expansions, and new programs.
Establish implementation plans, ownership, timelines, resource requirements, and success measures while managing operational readiness, risks, and dependencies.
Work with Medical Affairs, Finance, Talent & Culture, Marketing, Technology, Business Intelligence, Procurement, and Risk Management to ensure initiatives are adopted at clinic level and deliver measurable benefits.

A clear view of your assets

You bring progressive senior leadership experience overseeing a complex, geographically dispersed, multi-site organization.
You have successfully led regional or district leaders and delivered measurable operational improvements through local management teams.
You have experience in healthcare, ambulatory care, or another service environment with significant staffing, scheduling, and capacity requirements.
You demonstrate strong financial and analytical capabilities, including operational budgeting, forecasting, labour planning, and performance management.
You have built scalable operating practices and led organizational change through implementation and sustained adoption.
You have experience supporting acquisitions, integrations, or network expansion.
You hold a bachelor’s degree in business administration, healthcare management, operations, or a related field, or bring an equivalent combination of education and experience.

Your leadership approach

You build leaders: You develop capable teams, delegate effectively, and strengthen decision-making throughout the organization.
You drive performance: You understand operational and financial drivers, address performance gaps, and follow through on commitments.
You think systemically: You connect people, processes, capacity, technology, and patient needs when making decisions.
You lead change: You establish ownership, build commitment, and sustain new ways of working.
You influence effectively: You communicate clearly and build productive relationships with clinic teams, clinical partners, and executive leadership.
You exercise sound judgment: You balance patient care, employee experience, operational needs, and business performance.

From our point of view

This is an opportunity to shape how Vision Group’s clinic network operates and grows. You will develop leaders, strengthen execution, and build the operating model that supports our next stage of growth while keeping exceptional patient care at its centre.

If you bring the operational discipline, leadership, and vision to guide this next chapter, we invite you to apply.

jobs.title: Senior Director, SEM
jobs.description:
Please note that we will never request payment or bank account information at any stage of the recruitment process. As we continue to grow our teams, we urge you to be cautious of fraudulent job postings or recruitment activities that misuse our company name and information. Please protect your personal information during any recruitment process. While Monks may contact potential candidates via LinkedIn, all applications must be submitted through our official website (monks.com/careers).

About The Role

Search has changed more in the last two years than in the previous ten. Ads now run inside AI Overviews and AI Mode, keyword lists are giving way to AI Max and Performance Max, and conversational platforms like ChatGPT and Microsoft Copilot have opened as paid channels. We need a leader who sees that shift as an opportunity, not a threat.

As Senior Director, Paid Search, you will report to the VP of Paid Search and lead a group within the practice, owning performance, client relationships and talent across your book of business. You will lead a team from Account Managers through Directors, serve as paid search lead on one or two client accounts, and help define how Monks wins in an AI-first search landscape.

This is a senior leadership role: you run your accounts and team day to day, and support the VP and Group Directors in shaping the practice. Success means:

Your clients grow profitably, and we can prove the incremental impact of their search investment.
Your team operates at the frontier of AI-driven search, with clear points of view our clients and partners seek out.
Your book of business grows, through organic expansion on existing accounts and contributions to new business wins.
Your people develop into the next generation of search leaders.

Responsibilities

Strategy and AI leadership

Bring the practice's vision and roadmap, set by the VP and Group Directors, to life as strategy for your accounts, including how we plan, buy and measure across Google, Microsoft and emerging AI-driven ad surfaces.
Drive adoption of AI-powered campaign types, including AI Max for Search and Shopping, Performance Max, and AI Overviews and AI Mode placements. Build the playbooks, guardrails and testing frameworks the team uses to deploy them responsibly.
Shift the team's craft from manual execution to input governance: first-party data and conversion signals, feed quality, creative assets, brand guidelines and natural-language steering tools.
Evaluate and pilot new conversational ad channels, such as ChatGPT Ads and Microsoft Copilot placements, and advise clients on when and how to test them.
Author and publish agency POVs on the future of search, and support in award submissions and case studies.

Client leadership

Serve as paid search channel lead on one or two client accounts, owning search strategy, performance, day-to-day client communication and the account roadmap, while staying close to the platforms and the data.
Translate client business goals (revenue, profit, LTV, pipeline) into search strategies, and present them to VP- and Director-level client stakeholders, supporting C-suite presentations alongside the Group Director or VP.
Act as an escalation point and senior advisor across your group's accounts, stepping in to protect performance and relationships.
Partner with cross-channel leads (social, programmatic, retail media, SEO/GEO, analytics) on holistic media plans, including forecasting, budget allocation, testing and reporting.

Measurement and accountability

Champion measurement beyond platform-reported ROAS. Use incrementality testing, geo experiments and marketing mix modeling to prove and grow the value of search.
Ensure the team can explain performance clearly when platforms report less granular data, for example where AI Mode results are blended into campaign totals.
Own forecasting and scenario planning for your book of business.

People and practice leadership

Lead, develop and retain a team spanning Analysts through Directors. Set clear expectations, deliver regular feedback and run performance reviews.
Contribute to hiring, promotion and resourcing decisions for your team.
Upskill the team on AI tools and automation, so they spend less time on manual work and more on strategy, analysis and client value.
Build a culture of experimentation, knowledge sharing and accountability. Contribute to department-wide training and career frameworks.

Growth and commercial impact

Support new business pitches across SEM, Shopping and Performance Max, owning the search strategy component under the direction of the Group Director or VP.
Identify organic growth opportunities on existing accounts, including scope expansion, new markets and new channels.
Monitor account health and team utilization for your accounts, and flag scope, staffing and pricing needs to the VP.
Work closely with Google, Microsoft and other platform partners on beta tests, best practices and client planning.
Join in-person team meetings, client presentations and industry events as business needs arise, typically 1-2 times per quarter.

About You

The essentials:

8+ years of paid search experience, including senior leadership at an agency or in-house growth team.
3+ years of people management with at least 2 direct reports, ideally including Managers or Associate Directors.
Deep, hands-on expertise in Google Ads and Microsoft Advertising, including AI Max, Performance Max, Shopping and Smart Bidding.
Experience directing search portfolios of $1MM+ in monthly ad spend, with accountability for business outcomes, not just platform metrics.
A strong, well-reasoned POV on the future of search: AI-generated results, conversational ad surfaces, automation, and what they mean for agency value.
Working knowledge of modern measurement: conversion tracking and first-party data, incrementality and geo testing, and how MMM informs budget decisions.
A track record of presenting strategy to VP- and Director-level client stakeholders and large internal teams, with exposure to C-suite audiences.
Commercial awareness, including forecasting, scoping and spotting growth opportunities on existing accounts.
4-year college degree or equivalent work experience.

Not a Must, But a Plus

Hands-on testing of conversational ad platforms such as ChatGPT Ads or Microsoft Copilot ad formats.
Experience across YouTube, Demand Gen and App campaigns

jobs.title: SOX Director - ITGC
jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, which manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a SOX Director – ITGC based in Canada .

The SOX Director – ITGC will lead the strategy, design, and oversight of the enterprise IT SOX compliance program, serving as the senior technical authority for IT controls. This is a hands-on leadership role covering IT General Controls (ITGCs), IT Application Controls (ITACs), and controls related to private key management and digital asset custody. Operating in a complex, rapidly evolving financial technology environment, the successful candidate will build scalable control frameworks that support modern cloud infrastructure, continuous deployment, and blockchain-native systems without unnecessarily slowing engineering teams. The role requires close collaboration with Finance, Engineering, Security, Infrastructure, Internal Audit, and external auditors. It also carries significant executive visibility, including responsibility for communicating control risks, remediation progress, and the organization's overall IT control posture to senior leadership and the Audit Committee.

Accountabilities

Own the enterprise IT SOX strategy and roadmap, covering ITGCs, ITACs, and digital asset and private key management controls across relevant entities and jurisdictions.
Develop and maintain the IT SOX control framework, including scoping methodologies, risk assessments, control design standards, testing approaches, and evidence requirements.
Determine the applications, infrastructure, wallet and custody systems, third-party providers, and service-organization dependencies that fall within the SOX program's scope.
Design practical, effective controls that align with modern engineering environments, including cloud infrastructure, continuous integration and deployment (CI/CD), and infrastructure as code.
Establish standards for management testing and evidence quality, oversee co-sourced and matrixed resources, and review the quality and consistency of their work.
Introduce AI-enabled workflows, continuous controls monitoring, and data analytics to improve assurance efficiency and move beyond periodic manual testing.
Own SOX control design and coverage across the complete private key lifecycle, including key generation, storage, access, signing and approval workflows, rotation, backup, recovery, and retirement.
Assess controls over digital asset custody architectures, including hardware security modules (HSMs), multi-party computation (MPC), multi-signature arrangements, and hot, warm, and cold wallet structures.
Evaluate segregation of duties, quorum and approval requirements, privileged access, and other safeguards within key management and custody environments.
Assess how private key and custody controls support the existence, completeness, and safeguarding of customer and corporate digital assets, including their financial reporting implications.
Evaluate controls over on-chain and off-chain transaction processing, wallet-to-ledger reconciliations, blockchain data dependencies, and relationships with third-party custodians and service organizations.
Monitor emerging digital asset risks and adapt the SOX control framework as products, blockchain networks, and custody models evolve.
Lead the assessment of control deficiencies, including root cause analysis, severity and pervasiveness assessments, and recommendations for classification as control deficiencies, significant deficiencies, or material weaknesses.
Own remediation strategies for outstanding ITGC and key management findings, driving accountability and timely resolution with Engineering, Security, and Infrastructure leaders.
Escalate significant control gaps and remediation delays to senior leadership and report progress to the Audit Committee when required.
Coordinate with Internal Audit to ensure remediated controls are appropriately documented and ready for independent validation.
Serve as the senior SOX advisor to the CFO, CISO, CTO, Controller, and Audit Committee on IT control posture, emerging risks, and remediation priorities.
Lead external auditor engagement on IT matters, including audit strategy, scoping and reliance decisions, walkthroughs, and resolution of disagreements.
Advise Engineering and Security leaders by translating audit and compliance requirements into practical technical and operational control decisions.
Collaborate with Internal Audit, Enterprise Risk Management (ERM), business process SOX leaders, and co-sourced providers to coordinate coverage across the broader assurance program.
Mentor SOX and risk professionals, strengthening technical expertise and raising the overall quality of the function.

Requirements

Professional experience: 10+ years of experience in SOX compliance, IT audit, internal audit, or external audit, with deep ITGC expertise and a demonstrated record of leading enterprise-scale programs.
Mandatory crypto expertise: Direct, hands-on experience designing, assessing, or auditing controls related to cryptocurrency private key management, wallet infrastructure, signing workflows, digital asset custody, and asset safeguarding. This is an essential requirement.
Industry background: Experience in a cryptocurrency exchange, digital asset custodian, fintech, payments company, or similarly complex and rapidly evolving technology environment.
Certifications: CISA and CPA certifications are required. Candidates holding one certification and actively pursuing the other may also be considered.
SOX and audit frameworks: Expert knowledge of ITGC frameworks, SOX Section 404, COSO, COBIT, and PCAOB standards, with the ability to make and defend decisions involving control scope, audit reliance, and deficiency classification.
Technical understanding: Strong knowledge of systems architecture, databases, cloud infrastructure, deployment pipelines, and the technical environments supporting enterprise applications.
Financial reporting awareness: Ability to connect ITGC or private key management control failures to business process controls, financial reporting risks, and potential financial statement impacts.
Auditor and executive engagement: Experience managing relationships with external auditors, with Big Four experience preferred, and presenting control matters to Audit Committees and senior executives.
International experience: Experience working across multiple legal entities, jurisdictions, or complex organizational structures.
Leadership and communication: Strong stakeholder management, mentoring, and influencing skills, with the ability to establish credibility with both technical engineering teams and senior Finance leaders.
Preferred program experience: Experience establishing or scaling an IT SOX program in a growth-stage organization or a company entering its first year of SOX compliance.
Preferred technical knowledge: Familiarity with CI/CD processes, GitLab or comparable version-control platforms, and cloud environments such as AWS and Google Cloud Platform (GCP).
Third-party assurance: Familiarity with SOC 1 and SOC 2 reliance arrangements, third-party custodians, service providers, and proof-of-reserves or similar attestations.
Compliance technology: Experience with audit and governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) platforms such as AuditBoard or Workiva is an asset.
Emerging technologies: Familiarity with AI-assisted compliance tools and an interest in adopting new technologies to improve audit and assurance processes.

Benefits

Remote work: Full-time remote position, with Canada included among the eligible locations.
Annual target salary: USD $116,600–$259,700. The advertised range is a target annual salary range and may vary according to skills, experience, and the scope of the role.
Additional compensation: Eligibility for additional compensation through bonus and equity programs.
Wellness allowance: Additional wellness support is included in the compensation package.
Healthcare and retirement benefits: Medical, dental, vision, and 401(k) benefits are listed for eligible U.S. employees only; these should not be assumed to apply to Canadian employees.
Compensation flexibility: Final compensation is determined based on relevant experience, skills, and role responsibilities.
Global collaboration: Opportunity to work with international teams across Finance, Engineering, Security, and digital asset infrastructure.
Professional impact: Senior-level ownership of a complex SOX program, with direct exposure to executive leadership, external auditors, and emerging digital asset control challenges.

Our solutions foster the collaboration that’s critical for safer communities, safer schools, safer hospitals, safer businesses, and ultimately, safer nations. Connect with a career that matters, and help us build a safer future.

Chez Motorola Solutions, nous pensons que tout commence par nos employés. Nous sommes une communauté mondiale soudée, unie par la volonté incessante de contribuer à la sécurité des personnes partout dans le monde. Nous concevons et connectons des technologies qui contribuent à protéger les personnes, les biens et les infrastructures. Nos solutions favorisent la collaboration essentielle pour améliorer la sécurité des populations, des écoles, des hôpitaux, des entreprises et, finalement, des nations. Connectez-vous à une carrière qui compte et aidez-nous à bâtir un avenir plus sûr.

Department Overview

Motorola Solutions' innovations, products, and services play essential roles in people's lives. Our end-to-end suite of software solutions helps customers manage emergency communications, process video and evidence, and leverage cutting-edge AI-driven analytics for security and operational insights. We are industry leaders in video security and analytics, with solutions deployed in more than 120 countries across diverse environments such as school campuses, transportation systems, healthcare centers, public venues, critical infrastructure, prisons, factories, casinos, airports, financial institutions, government facilities, and retailers. Our AI-powered security solutions integrate advanced video analytics, machine learning, and embedded intelligence to enable proactive threat detection, enhanced situational awareness, and automated decision-making.

Job Description

Job DescriptionThe Director of Computer Vision will drive the technical vision, research and engineering execution for the platform, with focus on the following core areas:

Foundational Research Strategy: Define the long-term research agenda for fundamental computer vision capabilities and drive the culture of scientific excellence.
Technical Vision, Engineering Leadership, and Execution: Provide executive technical leadership to a unified research and engineering organization, defining the technical architecture, strategy, and engineering roadmap for the Computer Vision Platform. Drive execution, ensuring the seamless translation of product requirements into robust technical specifications and successful delivery of next-generation visual intelligence solutions that are highly scalable and align with overall product and business strategy.
Organizational Leadership and Talent Strategy: Manage and scale a unified computer vision research and engineering organization distributed across multiple geographies, overseeing multiple teams, and defining the strategy for recruiting, mentoring, and attracting world-class talent.
End-to-End MLOps and Deployment: Own the entire engineering lifecycle for central, reusable computer vision models and foundational AI infrastructure. This includes establishing best-in-class MLOps practices for scalable training, efficient deployment, continuous monitoring, and performance optimization across edge and cloud environments.
Performance Measurement and Continuous Improvement: Define, implement, and track key technical performance metrics (e.g., latency, throughput, model efficiency, system reliability) to measure engineering success, identify bottlenecks, and drive continuous improvement in execution and delivery.
Technical Innovation and Risk Management: Evaluate and integrate cutting-edge computer vision research and technologies. Proactively identify and mitigate significant technical risks, and lead critical engineering decisions, including build-versus-buy analysis.

Qualifications & Experience

10+ years of technical leadership experience leading computer vision teams and organizations, with a focus on building and deploying enterprise-scale platforms and solutions in production.
Technical Acumen & Deep Expertise: Deep, demonstrable expertise in computer vision, machine learning algorithms, and the end-to-end MLOps lifecycle, including 5+ years of hands-on experience building and optimizing computer vision models or as a computer vision researcher. Proven ability to engage in complex technical discussions, define the architectural vision for central, reusable AI infrastructure and models, and drive technical strategy while managing critical trade-offs.
Executive Technical Strategy & Metrics: Proven experience defining long-term technical vision, engineering strategy, and roadmaps for a large-scale platform. Expertise in defining and implementing technical metrics (e.g., latency, throughput, system reliability, model efficiency) to measure engineering excellence and drive continuous improvement across an organization.
Organizational & People Leadership: Demonstrated ability to manage and scale a unified, distributed engineering and research organization of 50 to 100 people, mentor senior technical talent, and lead multiple teams across different geographies.

new_jobs.title: Senior Director, SEM
new_jobs.description:
Please note that we will never request payment or bank account information at any stage of the recruitment process. As we continue to grow our teams, we urge you to be cautious of fraudulent job postings or recruitment activities that misuse our company name and information. Please protect your personal information during any recruitment process. While Monks may contact potential candidates via LinkedIn, all applications must be submitted through our official website (monks.com/careers).

About The Role

Search has changed more in the last two years than in the previous ten. Ads now run inside AI Overviews and AI Mode, keyword lists are giving way to AI Max and Performance Max, and conversational platforms like ChatGPT and Microsoft Copilot have opened as paid channels. We need a leader who sees that shift as an opportunity, not a threat.

As Senior Director, Paid Search, you will report to the VP of Paid Search and lead a group within the practice, owning performance, client relationships and talent across your book of business. You will lead a team from Account Managers through Directors, serve as paid search lead on one or two client accounts, and help define how Monks wins in an AI-first search landscape.

This is a senior leadership role: you run your accounts and team day to day, and support the VP and Group Directors in shaping the practice. Success means:

Your clients grow profitably, and we can prove the incremental impact of their search investment.
Your team operates at the frontier of AI-driven search, with clear points of view our clients and partners seek out.
Your book of business grows, through organic expansion on existing accounts and contributions to new business wins.
Your people develop into the next generation of search leaders.

Responsibilities

Strategy and AI leadership

Bring the practice's vision and roadmap, set by the VP and Group Directors, to life as strategy for your accounts, including how we plan, buy and measure across Google, Microsoft and emerging AI-driven ad surfaces.
Drive adoption of AI-powered campaign types, including AI Max for Search and Shopping, Performance Max, and AI Overviews and AI Mode placements. Build the playbooks, guardrails and testing frameworks the team uses to deploy them responsibly.
Shift the team's craft from manual execution to input governance: first-party data and conversion signals, feed quality, creative assets, brand guidelines and natural-language steering tools.
Evaluate and pilot new conversational ad channels, such as ChatGPT Ads and Microsoft Copilot placements, and advise clients on when and how to test them.
Author and publish agency POVs on the future of search, and support in award submissions and case studies.

Client leadership

Serve as paid search channel lead on one or two client accounts, owning search strategy, performance, day-to-day client communication and the account roadmap, while staying close to the platforms and the data.
Translate client business goals (revenue, profit, LTV, pipeline) into search strategies, and present them to VP- and Director-level client stakeholders, supporting C-suite presentations alongside the Group Director or VP.
Act as an escalation point and senior advisor across your group's accounts, stepping in to protect performance and relationships.
Partner with cross-channel leads (social, programmatic, retail media, SEO/GEO, analytics) on holistic media plans, including forecasting, budget allocation, testing and reporting.

Measurement and accountability

Champion measurement beyond platform-reported ROAS. Use incrementality testing, geo experiments and marketing mix modeling to prove and grow the value of search.
Ensure the team can explain performance clearly when platforms report less granular data, for example where AI Mode results are blended into campaign totals.
Own forecasting and scenario planning for your book of business.

People and practice leadership

Lead, develop and retain a team spanning Analysts through Directors. Set clear expectations, deliver regular feedback and run performance reviews.
Contribute to hiring, promotion and resourcing decisions for your team.
Upskill the team on AI tools and automation, so they spend less time on manual work and more on strategy, analysis and client value.
Build a culture of experimentation, knowledge sharing and accountability. Contribute to department-wide training and career frameworks.

Growth and commercial impact

Support new business pitches across SEM, Shopping and Performance Max, owning the search strategy component under the direction of the Group Director or VP.
Identify organic growth opportunities on existing accounts, including scope expansion, new markets and new channels.
Monitor account health and team utilization for your accounts, and flag scope, staffing and pricing needs to the VP.
Work closely with Google, Microsoft and other platform partners on beta tests, best practices and client planning.
Join in-person team meetings, client presentations and industry events as business needs arise, typically 1-2 times per quarter.

About You

The essentials:

8+ years of paid search experience, including senior leadership at an agency or in-house growth team.
3+ years of people management with at least 2 direct reports, ideally including Managers or Associate Directors.
Deep, hands-on expertise in Google Ads and Microsoft Advertising, including AI Max, Performance Max, Shopping and Smart Bidding.
Experience directing search portfolios of $1MM+ in monthly ad spend, with accountability for business outcomes, not just platform metrics.
A strong, well-reasoned POV on the future of search: AI-generated results, conversational ad surfaces, automation, and what they mean for agency value.
Working knowledge of modern measurement: conversion tracking and first-party data, incrementality and geo testing, and how MMM informs budget decisions.
A track record of presenting strategy to VP- and Director-level client stakeholders and large internal teams, with exposure to C-suite audiences.
Commercial awareness, including forecasting, scoping and spotting growth opportunities on existing accounts.
4-year college degree or equivalent work experience.

Not a Must, But a Plus

Hands-on testing of conversational ad platforms such as ChatGPT Ads or Microsoft Copilot ad formats.
Experience across YouTube, Demand Gen and App campaigns
Experience with bid management and reporting platforms such as SA360, Skai or Marin, plus BI tools like Looker or Tableau.
Familiarity with marketing mix modeling tools such as Google Meridian, or with designing geo-based incrementality experiments.
Experience leading strategy across B2B, D2C and B2C clients in multiple verticals, including regulated categories such as finance or healthcare.
Experience using AI and automation tools (scripts, LLM-based workflows, agentic tools) to scale team productivity.

This role is subject to our Return to Office (RTO) policy. If you reside within a commutable distance of one of our office locations, you will be expected to work from the office a set number of days per week. The specific details, including the number of required office days, will be in accordance with the company’s then-current RTO policy, which is subject to change from time to time.

Monks has provided a compensation range that represents its good faith estimate of what Monks may pay for the position at the time of posting. Monks may ultimately pay more or less than the posted compensation range. The salary offered to the selected candidate will be determined based on job-related factors, but not based on a candidate’s sex or any other protected status.

Salary Range$214,000—$240,000 CAD

About Monks

Monks is the global, digital-first, data-driven, unitary operating brand of S4Capital plc, where our culture centers on how we show up for the work and for one another. That begins with the commitment to strive for mastery—taking deep pride in our craft and creating work that sets the bar. In everyday execution, we drive momentum by choosing bold action rather than waiting for certainty. Above all, our teams are stronger together, bringing diverse perspectives into a unified team that communicates with clarity, trust, and mutual respect.

This commitment to craft and innovation translates directly into widespread industry acclaim: Monks was named a Contender in The Forrester Wave™: Global Marketing Services and a leader in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Global Digital Marketing Agencies. It ranks among Cannes Lions' Top 10 Creative Companies (2022-25) and remains the only partner featured in AdExchanger’s Programmatic Power Players list every year (2020-24). Named Adweek’s first AI Agency of the Year (2023) and The One Show’s inaugural AI Pioneer Organization (2025), Monks was also awarded Business Intelligence Group’s 2026 Excellence in Artificial Intelligence Award in the Human-Machine Interaction Team category. Additionally, Monks.Flow earned AI-based Marketing Solution of the Year at the 2026 AI Breakthrough Awards and a 2026 Global Generative AI Award in the Agentic Marketing Innovation category. Finally, Monks achieved a record-breaking number of FWAs and continues to hold the most of any partner.

We are an equal-opportunity employer committed to building a respectful and empowering work environment for all people to freely express themselves amongst colleagues who embrace diversity in all respects. Including fresh voices and unique points of view in all aspects of our business not only creates an environment where we can all grow and thrive but also increases our potential to produce work that better represents—and resonates with—the world around us.
